reviews.why: BHP's October 20 operational review confirmed Escondida's September disruption was real -- group copper output fell 19% to 400,700 tonnes and Escondida alone fell 23% to 252,600 tonnes -- but BHP left full-year guidance for both the group (1.65-1.80 million tonnes) and Escondida (1.00-1.10 million tonnes) unchanged, and the supervisors' agreement that took effect October 14 already removed the labor delay the thesis leaned on. Copper trades at $6.47/lb on October 23, little moved from two weeks ago, still well short of the September record and far from the $6.15 kill level, with no sign yet of the Sernageomin-driven restart delay the variant expected.

no_new_call_note: A scan across commodities, crypto and stocks this week turned up nothing both new and confirmed by more than one independent source that the market has not already priced: China's rare-earth export truce, OPEC+'s unchanged October quota and the ongoing wait on sixteen crypto ETF decisions are each already reported and already reflected in price, so no new call opens this week.
